title: 薄荷叶之间  (Between the Mint Leaves)

segments.t: On the sunlit table inside Room Nine, Mei lays the top half of the torn recipe card beside the open green botanical book while Teacher Song and Manager Zhou lean over the pressed pages. Let us listen in first.
快看这两枝压干的花园薄荷和香草中间。
书脊旁边平平地夹着半张撕破的米色卡片！
小美，把它推到时间胶囊那一半旁边——边角对得上吗？
每一丝纸边都对得清清楚楚，像破茶杯的两半拼在一起！
小美，把烤蛋糕的菜谱大声念出来，我好工工整整抄下来。
把整颗莓果轻轻拌进杏仁面糊，烤四十分钟直到金黄。
太好了！听起来挺简单嘛——小美，你干吗眯着眼看最后一行？
因为一大滴雨点正好落在秘密热糖霜的蓝墨水上！
让我戴上老花镜看看：趁热在蛋糕上刷两勺……蓝水痕！
宋老师，蓝水痕可不是星期六集市上买得到的材料呀！
老板别慌；蛋糕底我们有了，我的厨房就来试三种糖霜！
星期天下午连烤三个蛋糕尝尝？这种历史研究我一百个支持！
Now let's go through it line by line with the English translation.
快看这两枝压干的花园薄荷和香草中间。

'Look right between these two pressed dry sprigs of garden mint and sweet herbs.' Slender stems and sprigs take the counter "zhi", while "ya gan" links "press" with "dry" for herbs flattened inside a book.
书脊旁边平平地夹着半张撕破的米色卡片！

'Tucked flat against the spine of the book is half of a torn cream card!' "Shuji" pictures a book's spine as its "book-backbone", and "jia" means pressing or tucking something snugly between two pages.
小美，把它推到时间胶囊那一半旁边——边角对得上吗？
'Slide it beside the half from the time capsule, Mei—do the edges match?' Dropping "de" inside "dui shang" builds "dui de shang", asking whether the two torn edges can actually line up.
每一丝纸边都对得清清楚楚，像破茶杯的两半拼在一起！

'Every tiny paper fibre lines up cleanly, like two halves of a broken teacup pieced together!' "Si" names a hair-fine thread or paper fibre, and "pin zai yiqi" means fitting separate pieces back together as one.
小美，把烤蛋糕的菜谱大声念出来，我好工工整整抄下来。
'Read the cake baking recipe aloud, Mei, so I can copy it down nice and neatly.' "Caipu" names a recipe, and "chao xialai" pairs "copy" with "down" for writing words onto fresh paper to keep.
把整颗莓果轻轻拌进杏仁面糊，烤四十分钟直到金黄。
'Fold whole berries gently into the almond batter and bake forty minutes until golden.' Small round berries take the counter "ke", while "mianhu" combines "flour" and "paste" for smooth cake batter.
太好了！听起来挺简单嘛——小美，你干吗眯着眼看最后一行？

'Wonderful! That sounds simple enough—why are you squinting at the bottom line, Mei?' Read "hang" rather than "xing", this character counts rows of writing, making "zuihou yi hang" "the very last line".
因为一大滴雨点正好落在秘密热糖霜的蓝墨水上！

'Because one big raindrop landed right on the blue ink for the secret warm glaze!' "Yi da di yudian" counts one fat raindrop with "di" ("drop"), and "tangshuang" literally means "sugar-frost"—cake glaze.
让我戴上老花镜看看：趁热在蛋糕上刷两勺……蓝水痕！

'Let me look through my reading glasses: while warm, brush the cake with two spoons of... blue water stain!' Two brisk syllables, "chen re", mean "while it is still warm", and "shuihen" joins "water" and "mark" for a stain.
宋老师，蓝水痕可不是星期六集市上买得到的材料呀！

'Blue water stain is definitely not an ingredient you can buy at the Saturday market, Teacher Song!' Emphatic "ke" before "bu shi" sharpens Zhou's joke—"is certainly not!"—while "mai de dao" means "able to buy".
老板别慌；蛋糕底我们有了，我的厨房就来试三种糖霜！

'Do not panic, boss; we have the cake base now, so my kitchen will test three kinds of glaze!' Mei fronts the topic "dangao di" ("cake base") first—"as for the cake base, we have it"—before launching her kitchen plan.
星期天下午连烤三个蛋糕尝尝？这种历史研究我一百个支持！

'Bake three test cakes in a row on a Sunday afternoon? Now that kind of historical research I support a hundredfold!' Saying "yibai ge zhichi"—literally "one hundred supports"—is an exuberant spoken way to back an idea wholeheartedly.
Now let's listen to the whole conversation one last time.
快看这两枝压干的花园薄荷和香草中间。

星期天下午连烤三个蛋糕尝尝？这种历史研究我一百个支持！
The torn card fits together cleanly, leaving only one raindrop-stained secret glaze for Mei and her oven to solve! See you next time.
下次见！
